displayText: Last change: stretch the curve upwards. Three e to the x makes every height three times taller. Look at the tangent triangle. The run doesn't change, but the rise is three times bigger, so the slope is three times steeper. That's the Year 11 constant multiple rule: the three comes along for the ride. And notice, the gradient still equals the height, because both grew by the same factor of three. So k scales everything, but only a changes the gradient compared with the height.
